steps.label: Strong consistency
steps.sub: every read sees the latest write, everywhere

steps.label: Eventual consistency
steps.sub: replicas converge over time; reads may be briefly stale

steps.label: The trade
steps.sub: eventual buys lower latency and higher availability

steps.label: Basically Available
steps.sub: responds most of the time, even during failures

steps.label: Soft state
steps.sub: data can change over time as replicas converge

eyebrow: Two writes, same key, same moment

steps.label: Last-write-wins
steps.sub: keep the newest timestamp; simple but can lose data

steps.label: Version vectors
steps.sub: detect true concurrency instead of guessing

steps.label: CRDTs
steps.sub: data structures that merge concurrent updates automatically

code:
1. You update a DNS A record
2. Authoritative server has the new value immediately
3. Resolvers worldwide still serve cached old value
4. Each cache expires at its TTL
5. Eventually every resolver converges on the new value
caption: DNS propagation: a familiar, real-world eventual-consistency system.
